findings.reason: the plan fixes no interface budget for the shared writer, so a section adding surface can absorb arbitrary per-caller knobs uncriticised; naming the budget (which knobs are the writer's own, which callers must change instead) would change §3's deliverable.
findings.text: `write_json_atomically` now carries seven keyword arguments whose only purpose is to let each migrating caller keep the exact serialization, permission, durability and parent-creation behaviour it had before migration, so the interface grows monotonically with the number of callers and a reader cannot tell which combination is the supported writer from which is a legacy quirk

findings.reason: the design must either eliminate the delegate (callers take the function-local import themselves) or state the constraint and change the done-when, because as written the measure can never pass while the delegates remain.
findings.text: `_run_streams(path)` is a pure forward to `metering.run_streams(path)` adding no behaviour, kept only so a module-level import of `reckon.crew.metering` is not required, but the plan's §3 done-when asserts the census will report "one implementation per concept" and never states the circular-import constraint that forces the delegate

findings.reason: the plan should name and migrate `reports._instant` (the fence-expiry judge, landed after the census pin) and state that the census must enumerate every direct caller before its "at most three" bound means anything.
findings.text: `_instant` reads an ISO-8601 `Z` stamp with `datetime.fromisoformat(text).timestamp()` directly, duplicating `reckon/_timestamps.py:parse_utc`, and the plan's census at the migration pin names seven remaining `fromisoformat` callers but not this one, so a private timestamp parser exists outside the owner the plan declares

findings.reason: the design's writer inventory is the scope of §3, and a JSON writer the census cannot see is a duplicate the section claims to end; the plan should either widen the detector's pattern set or name this caller as an exception with its reason.
findings.text: `_write_settings` writes its JSON through `write_bytes` into a unique sibling with a chmod and `os.replace`, duplicating the atomic-write owner `reckon/_store.py:write_json_atomically`, and the plan's detector looks for `write`/`write_text` and so never lists it as a caller

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the shared writer's interface grew one keyword knob per migration wave (fsync, indent, sort_keys, mode, fsync_directory, create_parents, ensure_ascii) so each caller configures the owner to reproduce its own prior behaviour, moving per-caller behaviour into the interface rather than hiding it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan's census-scoped search never reaches `reckon/crew/reports.py:1675 _instant`, a private ISO-8601 parser duplicating the module the plan creates (`reckon/_timestamps.py:parse_utc`), and it also never names the atomic writer in `reckon/hooks/install.py:362 _write_settings`, which duplicates `reckon/_store.py:write_json_atomically`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the codebase it names, citing the structural census and the crew pattern review, and the code confirms it extends existing owners (`reckon/_store.py`'s sibling-temporary writer, `reckon/crew/metering.py:run_streams`) rather than adding parallel machinery; `write_json_atomically` reuses `_write_through_sibling_temporary` (reckon/_store.py:419) shared with the pre-existing envelope writer.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3's stream enumeration leaves `reckon/crew/promotion.py:3397` and `reckon/ledger.py:3154` as forwards to `metering.run_streams` while the done-when claims "one implementation per concept", and the plan never states why the owner cannot be called directly; the reason (function-local import avoids the `reckon.crew` facade circular import) lives only in a code comment.
